territorial_scope.description: Applies to paid advertisements relating to federal, state or local candidates and elections in Michigan, and to Michigan ballot questions.

evidence.quote: relating to a candidate for federal, state, or local office in this state

summary.short: Amends Michigan Campaign Finance Act section 47 and adds section 59, requiring that political advertisements and prerecorded telephone messages generated in whole or substantially by artificial intelligence carry a disclosure statement. Covers Michigan candidates, elections and ballot questions; violations carry civil fines or misdemeanor penalties.
summary.long: Amends section 47 of the Michigan Campaign Finance Act and adds section 59. Section 59 requires a person, committee or other entity that creates, originally publishes or originally distributes a qualified political advertisement (a paid advertisement relating to a federal, state or local candidate or election in Michigan, or a ballot question, containing AI-generated image, audio or video) to state that it was generated in whole or substantially by artificial intelligence, with minimum size, duration and language rules for graphic, audio and video formats. A first violation is a state civil infraction with a fine of up to $250; later violations carry up to $1,000 each, and each distribution is a separate violation. Exemptions cover bona fide news coverage, paid broadcasts, satire or parody, businesses regulated by the Michigan Public Service Commission or the FCC, and distribution platforms with a written disclosure policy; platforms are not liable for missing disclosures if they gave notice of their prohibitions. Section 47 requires AI-generated prerecorded telephone messages advocating for or against a candidate or ballot question to carry a specified statement. Knowing violations of section 47 are misdemeanors punishable by a fine of up to $1,000, imprisonment for up to 93 days, or both. The amendments do not take effect unless House Bill 5143 of the 102nd Legislature is enacted into law.

notes: Target act 1976 PA 388 is not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is left empty. The text does not state a legal basis, enacting bill, repeal or replacement; the Public Act and enrolled bill numbers come from registry metadata, not the document. Sec. 47(1), (5) and (7) cross-refer internally to section 55 and section 6(2)(j) of 1976 PA 388, which are not reproduced. The amended section 47 is printed without marking new text, so new and restated language cannot be told apart. Inconsistency: Sec. 59(5) and 59(4)(c) refer to failures to disclose AI content in a prerecorded telephone message, but Sec. 59(1) and the Sec. 59(6) definition cover only qualified political advertisements; the prerecorded-message AI disclaimer is in Sec. 47(7), with different wording. Sec. 47 and Sec. 59 may both reach AI-generated political ads, and the text does not say how they interact. Effectiveness depends on House Bill 5143 (102nd Legislature), which was not checked.
